node: Warehouse robotics, store automation, and fulfillment productivity systems
summary: Expanded the node beyond obvious warehouse-robot vendors into software execution layers, retail trading-network plumbing, RFID/data-capture hardware, and automation platforms. The most direct reference name is Symbotic because of disclosed Walmart automation agreements. The underfollowed lane is more interesting in SPS Commerce, Manhattan Associates, and Zebra Technologies, where exposure sits one or two steps away from consumer e-commerce labels: supplier-retailer integration, omnichannel warehouse execution, inventory visibility, RFID, mobile computing, and store/warehouse workflow automation. These are not buy/sell conclusions; they are Layer 1B research candidates requiring later validation of customer concentration, backlog, deployment cadence, margin quality, service obligations, and whether automation budgets remain protected in a softer consumer environment.
